answer: An attacker runs a phone farm on a knoll, minting 200 fakes. Each identity must lock a 60-POA bond to one geographic vertex — a cell-tower point — and post an opal beacon proof: a signed signal reading each epoch. One identity per vertex, so each extra fake needs a new vertex, device and bond. The bond grows: the k-th identity costs 60×k POA — the 1st 60, the 10th 600, the 100th 6,000; 100 fakes lock 303,000 POA together. Audits re-check 1 in 8 vertices each epoch; a failed reading slashes the bond and freezes the account 6 epochs. Honest users keep one cheap bond; farms pay super-linear rent.
